# December Documentation

December is a (so much) better coding agent for terminal and cloud. It understands your codebase and helps you build faster by writing code, fixing bugs, and running commands. Use it directly in your terminal or alongside your favorite IDE.

**Also available on the web at [trydecember.com](https://trydecember.com)**

- **Writes code & runs commands:** Ask it to build features, fix bugs, or run tests. It does the work for you.
- **Cloud Handoff:** Use _/handoff_ to continue your session on **[trydecember.com](https://trydecember.com)**
- **Bring your own AI:** Use API keys for OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, and 150+ others, or log in via December to use December credits.

- Website: https://trydecember.com
- Repository: https://github.com/phasehumans/december
- CLI Package: @trydecember/cli (npm)

---

## 1. Get Started

1. Install December:

```bash
npm install -g @trydecember/cli
```

2. Navigate to your project directory and run `december`.

### Additional Install Options
```bash
bun add -g @trydecember/cli
pnpm add -g @trydecember/cli
```

### Setup
```bash
# Log in to December Cloud (optional, enables cloud handoff and previews)
december login

# Pick your model provider and add API keys
december config
```

### Running Tasks
```bash
# Run a single task
december "fix failing unit tests in packages/server"

# Start an interactive terminal session
december
```

### Flags
- `--model <name>`: Model to use (e.g. `claude-3-5-sonnet-latest`, `gpt-4o`, `gemini-2.0-flash`).
- `--temperature <num>`: Temperature (default: `0.2`).
- `--verbose`: Show full reasoning and tool output.
- `--checkpoint`: Make a git checkpoint after every file edit.
- `--steer`: Ask before making file edits or running bash commands.

---

## 2. Slash Commands

Use these commands inside an interactive `december` session:

- `/handoff`: Move current task, diffs, and chat history to a cloud sandbox.
- `/checkpoint [message]`: Save a git commit on the shadow branch.
- `/undo`: Revert the last file edits made by the agent.
- `/diff`: Show uncommitted changes.
- `/clear`: Clear conversation history.
- `/model`: Switch models mid-session.
- `/help`: List all commands.

---

## 3. Architecture

December has three parts:

### 3.1 Terminal CLI
- Node.js CLI tool.
- Reads project files and runs edits locally.
- Creates git commits on a shadow branch so you can undo changes at any time.

### 3.2 API Server
- Node.js backend.
- Manages user sessions, encrypted keys, and WebSocket streaming between CLI and cloud.

### 3.3 Cloud Sandboxes
- Isolated Linux microVMs (E2B / Firecracker).
- Runs commands in disposable containers.
- Generates live web preview URLs with port forwarding.

---

## 4. Agent Loop

December runs a 5-step loop:
1. **Inspect**: Read files, search symbols, check git diffs.
2. **Plan**: Pick the smallest set of edits needed.
3. **Execute**: Call tools (`view_file`, `replace_file_content`, `write_to_file`, `run_command`).
4. **Verify**: Run tests or compiler (`tsc`, `npm test`) to check work.
5. **Checkpoint**: Commit verified edits before moving to the next step.

---

## 5. Supported Models (BYOK)

Bring your own API keys for 150+ providers:
- **Anthropic**: Claude 3.5 Sonnet, Claude 3.5 Haiku, Claude 3 Opus.
- **OpenAI**: GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini, o1.
- **Google**: Gemini 2.0 Flash, Gemini 1.5 Pro.
- **DeepSeek**: DeepSeek-V3, DeepSeek-R1.
- **Groq**: Fast open-weights inference (Llama 3.3 70B, Qwen 2.5 Coder).
- **Ollama**: Run offline on `localhost:11434`.

---

## 6. Privacy & Security

- **No Training**: Your code is never used to train models.
- **Disposable Sandboxes**: Cloud microVMs are destroyed when a task ends.
- **Secret Masking**: `.env` files and API keys are automatically hidden from logs.
- **Runs Locally**: You can run 100% locally with your own API key.

### What is December?
December is a coding agent that lives in your terminal. It understands your codebase and helps you build faster by writing code, fixing bugs, and running commands. Use it directly in your terminal or alongside your favorite IDE.

### How does December compare to Cursor or Devin?
Unlike Cursor (which is a VS Code fork), December runs directly in your existing terminal and works with any editor (Neovim, VS Code, JetBrains). Unlike Devin, December can run 100% locally with zero latency, handing off to the cloud only when you want background runs or shareable previews.

### How does terminal-to-cloud handoff work?
Run `/handoff` in your terminal. December sends your uncommitted diffs and session history to a cloud microVM. You get a URL to continue the task in your browser.
